- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent history, model tends to under-forecast early spikes; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for the first 3–5 days after sentiment shift.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often over-estimates continuation; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment remains flat (0.00) for 5+ days, model exhibits mean reversion bias — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment shifts.
- Model consistently under-forecasts true price peaks in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If model forecast is below 70.00 and sentiment is flat, avoid downward bias — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment or price breaks above 71.00.
